item.title: Zeppelin Rigid Keel Dream
item.description: Name the aluminium frame, not just the hydrogen. On 31 August 1895 Zeppelin got the patent for a navigable rigid airship — aluminium skeleton, hydrogen cells, two Daimler hearts, a rudder that finally steered the sky instead of drifting with it. Before the rigid frame every balloon was a floppy sack; after it the sky had a spine. Tonight’s Apple lane is not more M6 slogans; it is mini/Studio enterprise AI demand forcing the calendar while GTM lags — multi-Studio linking pitch, PCC still not for sale, DRAM stockouts spilling buyers toward Nvidia DGX Spark. Local lane: Ollama v0.33.2 stays the frozen keel pin; llama.cpp b10709 is optional rivet cadence; production still holds the multi-day vLLM 0.28.0 / OWUI 0.11.1 floors. New gondola: arXiv→NotebookLM podcast pipeline is built and anomalous as hell (σ≈10.77) but still blocked on one-time Google auth on this Safari-only mini — frame without boarding pass. Workstation copper: Mac Studio flipped to M5 Max $2,499 / M5 Ultra $5,499. Yesterday a grey shale slab with soft Cambrian animals. Tonight a cigar of aluminium ribs over Lake Constance. Your job is not more lift — it is which surfaces still float as floppy balloons, which pins are keels, and which gondolas still need the pass before the props bite.

item.title: Burgess Shale Bestiary Dream
item.description: Name the soft fauna, not just the trilobite label. Tonight’s Apple lane is not more M6 slogans; it is Parallels Desktop 27 putting SME2 under Linux/Windows VMs so Ollama and llama.cpp run inside the guest with Jamf and golden images attached, CarPlay shipping a fourth third-party chatbot before personal Siri AI GA, oMLX 0.6.4 continuous batching on private Macs, and MLX Metal correctness still open on OOB/GQA after the strided-scan fix. Local lane: Ollama v0.33.2 stays the frozen type specimen (HEAD identical); llama.cpp b10688 is optional soft-tissue cadence; production still holds the multi-day vLLM 0.28.0 / OWUI 0.11.1 floors. Yesterday a small iron ring under oil light, two coils, one astonished needle. Tonight a grey shale slab on a mountain bench, five weird successful animals, a peeling trilobite drawer label. Your job is not a harder shell — it is which soft forms only show under exceptional conditions, which hard labels erase them, and which production pins are the type specimens you keep while the catalog rewrites.

Your job is not a longer spark — it is which winding you meant to energize, which only answers, and which production keys still click when the meter goes quiet.

item.title: Krakatoa Barometer Dream
item.description: Treat the blast as a receipt, not a demo. On 26 August 1883 Krakatoa began the fold that left the loudest sound in human history — no local mic, only barometers looping the pressure seven times around the planet. Same calendar square in 1928: an opaque ginger-beer bottle and a snail that was never exhibited still rewired who owes whom what down the supply chain. Tonight Ollama v0.33.0 finally GA’d after the rc hangover; Open WebUI v0.11.1 is the force-upgrade wave that has to circle the fleet; Apple published the M6 mini and M5 Ultra 512GB private-inference matrix instead of another sky story. Beehiiv can wait — the six people already on the list are the neighbours through dark glass. Yesterday a brass eyepiece you control. Tonight a barometer that keeps counting loops, and a bottle you still owe even when you cannot see inside. Your job is not a louder demo — it is which blasts leave planetary receipts, which bottles still hide snails, and who you call neighbour when the glass is dark.

item.title: Great Moon Hoax Eyepiece Dream
item.description: Own the eyepiece before you trust the moon story. In 1835 the New York Sun printed bat-people on the Moon and sold every copy because the form looked trustworthy. Yesterday a dwarf planet that kept spinning after the club redrew the line. Tonight a brass-rimmed telescope you control, and a newspaper that invented the sky. Your job is not another sky story — it is which claims are 1835 Moon bats, which are brass instruments under your finger, and who owns the reveal button.

item.title: Still There Moon Dream
item.description: What you press into the fleet tonight is still there in fifty-seven years of silence.** Genius Bar Live Notes, Ollama pins, Metal buffer bugs, dual-consent transcripts — no weather sands them. If your Mac AI policy can't answer retention, HR use, and edit-before-save for a Genius Bar-style capture, you're not ready for on-device meeting AI either. Freeze Ollama on v0.32.1. Treat the $88M funding blog as roadmap review, not a pin change. Continuous-batching soak tests — not homepage tok/s — decide Mac Studio fleet pins. Design the footprint like the Moon is watching.

item.title: Six Days Rome Fire Dream
item.description: When half the city is glowing, stop asking whether the fire is "allowed." Ask which districts you meant to lose, who owns the wind (cache / concurrency / kill switch), and whether tonight's story is a real instrument or a fiddle invented after the ash.

item.title: Perfect Ten Scoreboard Dream
item.description: When the board says 1.00, the routine already stuck.** Don't freeze forever on the glitch frame — and don't auto-track mainline that invents new digits before the fleet can display them. Pin Ollama on v0.32.1. Treat dual-vendor + App Store + dugout-iPad rules as scoreboard firmware work. Device approval is not AI approval. Production pin is not mainline. The perfect score arrives as a bug report.
